subject: Physics
q: Two solid spheres have radii R₁ = 1 m and R₂ = 2 m and masses M₁ and M₂, respectively. Their gravitational-field-versus-radius graphs reach surface values E₁ = 2 and E₂ = 3 in the same units. What is M₁/M₂?
imgAlt: Field-radius graph: sphere 1 peaks at E=2 when r=1 m; sphere 2 peaks at E=3 when r=2 m
hint: At a sphere's surface, the gravitational field is GM/R².
solution: At each surface, E = GM/R², so M is proportional to ER². Therefore M₁/M₂ = (E₁R₁²)/(E₂R₂²) = (2 × 1²)/(3 × 2²) = 1/6.
